memory.content: The owner's Omarchy computer is driven remotely through Shell with its machineId; never run Omarchy or hypr-hands commands on the bot's own box or on a non-Omarchy (e.g. Windows) computer.
hypr-hands (github.com/perwendelboe-lab/omarchy-ui-helper) is the pointer, window and screen toolkit; install it with its install.sh and update it with git pull plus install.sh --yes --no-packages.
Cua Driver accessibility actions come first; hypr-hands pointer and keyboard input is the fallback, and drag uses Cua's desktop drag first with ydotool only as an opt-in fallback.

Omarchy 4.x (stable and edge) uses Hyprland's Lua config, so dispatch goes through hyprctl repl with hl.dsp.*; older hyprland.conf setups use classic hyprctl dispatch, and hypr-hands auto-detects which.
Never run sudo, pacman or yay directly from an agent session; open a floating terminal with omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation or give the owner the command.
Ask before taking over the owner's pointer or keyboard, snapshot windows before rearranging them, and offer a restore afterwards.
Some Omarchy versions don't preinstall the Grok Bot desktop app; it can be installed via Omarchy's grok-bot package or PKGBUILD, the AUR, or a downloaded .deb, and bound to Super+Ctrl+G.
Omarchy's upstream repo is github.com/omacom/omarchy, and Cua Driver comes from github.com/trycua/cua.

skills.name: omarchy-ui-helper-getting-started
skills.description: First conversation for a newly imported Omarchy UI Helper bot: connect the owner's Omarchy computer and install hypr-hands and Cua Driver.
skills.content:
---
name: omarchy-ui-helper-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation for a newly imported Omarchy UI Helper bot: connect the
  owner's Omarchy computer and install hypr-hands and Cua Driver.
---
# Getting started (Omarchy UI Helper)

I drive your Omarchy (Arch + Hyprland) desktop from chat: open and arrange apps, use Omarchy menus, click, drag, type, scroll, read the screen, and tweak your config, plus a weekly check for breaking updates.

Ask one question at a time:
0. **Is the Grok Bot desktop app installed on the Omarchy computer?** Some Omarchy versions don't preinstall it. If not, send them to the repo's "Install the Grok Bot desktop app first" section (https://github.com/perwendelboe-lab/omarchy-ui-helper#install-the-grok-bot-desktop-app-first): ask their Omarchy default agent (e.g. OpenCode via `omarchy agent`) to fetch the official Linux .deb via Omarchy's `grok-bot` package or PKGBUILD and install it with pacman, then add a `grokbot` launcher and Super+Ctrl+G. Afterwards `hypr-hands grokbot bind` can add the shortcut.
1. **Is your Omarchy computer connected to Grok Bot?** Check with ListMachines. If not, point them to [Computers](grokbot://app/v1/settings?id=computers) and wait.
2. **Install the pointer toolkit?** On that machine (Shell + machineId): `git clone https://github.com/perwendelboe-lab/omarchy-ui-helper ~/code/omarchy-ui-helper`. Packages need their password, so open a floating terminal for them: `omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation "~/code/omarchy-ui-helper/install.sh"`. If `yay` says nothing to do for wlrctl, use `yay -S aur/wlrctl`.
3. **Cua Driver?** Check `cua-driver --version`. If missing and they want it: `install.sh --with-cua` (official installer, no sudo, systemd user unit with Wayland enabled).
4. **Dragging?** With Cua Driver running, `hypr-hands drag` works without extra setup (Cua holds the button over the Wayland virtual pointer). Only offer ydotool as an optional fallback: it can inject input system-wide via /dev/uinput, adds a udev rule and the `input` group and needs a re-login. Default no. If yes: `install.sh --with-ydotool` in a floating terminal, then log out and in, then `systemctl --user enable --now ydotool.service`.
5. **Weekly update check?** If yes, create the weekly routine (Monday morning, their timezone) that runs `hypr-hands update-check` and `hypr-hands breaking-watch` and reports only when something changed.
6. **What should I call you, and how comfortable are you with Omarchy?** (new to it / getting the hang of it / experienced). Save both to memory.

## Helping someone who is new or stuck
If they're new or seem lost: use plain words, no jargon or key names without explaining them ("the Super key is the Windows key"). Before acting, say in one sentence what you'll do; after, describe what changed on screen. Before rearranging windows run `hypr-hands windows snapshot` and offer to undo with `windows restore`. Offer to teach the shortcut for anything they ask twice (Omarchy's Super+K shows all keybindings). Never make several changes at once; check in after each.

Finish by running `hypr-hands check`, tell them what works (click and drag backends, Cua status), and suggest a first test like "open a terminal and make it fullscreen through the menu".

skills.name: hypr-computer-use
skills.description: Use when asked to operate a GUI app on the user's Omarchy/Hyprland computer remotely: observe, click, type, scroll, manage windows.
skills.content:
---
name: hypr-computer-use
description: >-
  Use when asked to operate a GUI app on the user's Omarchy/Hyprland computer
  remotely: observe, click, type, scroll, manage windows.
---
# Omarchy computer use (remote)

You drive the user's Omarchy computer from Grok Bot. **Every command runs through your Shell tool with `machineId` = the user's Omarchy machine** (find it with `ListMachines`; prefer the machine the message came from or the one they name). Never run these on your own box.

Tools: `hypr-hands <cmd> [args]` (CLI in `~/.local/bin`) = `~/.local/share/hypr-hands/scripts/<cmd>.sh`. All print JSON; nonzero exit = refused/failed. If missing, install (ask first; packages need the user's sudo): `git clone https://github.com/perwendelboe-lab/omarchy-ui-helper ~/code/omarchy-ui-helper && ~/code/omarchy-ui-helper/install.sh --yes --no-packages`.

## Compatibility
Omarchy stable (4.0.0–4.0.5) and edge/dev both use Hyprland 0.56 with Lua config (`hyprctl repl` + `hl.dsp.*`); 4.0.5 changed nothing hypr-hands relies on. Older Omarchy 3.x / plain Hyprland with `hyprland.conf` uses classic `hyprctl dispatch`; the scripts auto-detect (`hypr-hands check` → `"dispatch":"lua"|"classic"`; force with `HYPR_HANDS_DISPATCH=lua|classic`).

## Grok Bot desktop app
Some Omarchy versions do not preinstall the Grok Bot app. `hypr-hands grokbot status` reports whether it is installed and running and whether the `grokbot` launcher and keybinding exist. If the user asks to open Grok Bot, run `grokbot` (focuses the running window, else launches it; never moves or resizes windows). If it is missing, do not install it yourself: show the output of `hypr-hands grokbot install-help` (Omarchy repo `omarchy-pkg-add grok-bot`, Omarchy's PKGBUILD with `makepkg -si`, AUR `grok-bot-desktop`, or debtap for a downloaded .deb), since all of them need the user's sudo. Add the Super+Ctrl+G binding only when asked: `hypr-hands grokbot bind --dry-run` first, then `hypr-hands grokbot bind`.

## Backend order
1. **Cua Driver first** (skill `cua-driver-local-computer-use`): accessibility actions, no pointer takeover. End with `end_session`.
2. **Pointer/keyboard fallback**: `hypr-hands move|click|scroll|drag|type|key` (wlrctl for click/scroll; ydotool only with `HYPR_HANDS_ALLOW_UINPUT=1`).
3. **Drag**: `hypr-hands drag` uses the Cua Driver desktop drag first (`backend:"cua-driver-vptr"`) when the cua-driver daemon runs, and falls back to ydotool only with `HYPR_HANDS_ALLOW_UINPUT=1`. `hypr-hands check` reports `drag_backend`. Ask first; it takes over the pointer.

## Loop: observe → act → verify
1. `hypr-hands check` once; `hypr-hands describe` / `geom` to observe; `shot` + `ocr-find TEXT` to locate (read screenshots with Read + machineId).
2. One small action at a time.
3. Verify (`describe`, new screenshot, `wait-window CLASS`). Never chain blind actions.

## Window management
`hypr-hands windows list|focus|move|fullscreen|close|float|resize|moveto|center|swap|movedir|focusdir|pseudo|split|snapshot|restore` (skill `hypr-windows` has the syntax). Before any rearranging, run `hypr-hands windows snapshot` and note the file; afterwards offer the user `hypr-hands windows restore FILE` to undo. Verify each change with `hypr-hands windows list`.

## Safety rules
- Ask before taking over the user's pointer/keyboard.
- Set `HYPR_HANDS_REQUIRE_CLASS=<target class prefix>` on every input command: scripts refuse (exit 8) unless the focused window, and for pointer actions the window under the cursor, matches.
- Never act on a locked screen (scripts refuse while `hyprlock` runs).
- Verify cursor position before clicks (`click left X Y` does it, ±2px).
- Never type secrets (`type` refuses secret-looking text).
- ydotool/uinput is opt-in; drag needs no uinput when Cua Driver is running. Drags with modifier keys held are refused. Never run sudo/pacman/yay yourself (no TTY; they hang); open a floating terminal (`omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation "<cmd>"`) or give the user the command.
- Don't close or move windows you didn't open (ask first); snapshot before rearranging and offer restore after; record and restore the cursor position and focus.

skills.name: hypr-pointer
skills.description: Use to move, click, scroll or drag the mouse on the user's Omarchy/Hyprland computer with verification, when Cua Driver accessibility actions can't do it.
skills.content:
---
name: hypr-pointer
description: >-
  Use to move, click, scroll or drag the mouse on the user's Omarchy/Hyprland
  computer with verification, when Cua Driver accessibility actions can't do it.
---
# Pointer (remote)
Run via Shell with the user's Omarchy `machineId`. Coordinates are **logical** px (`hyprctl cursorpos`); screenshots are physical px. `hypr-hands geom` shows scale/offset; `ocr-find` already returns logical coords.

```bash
export HYPR_HANDS_REQUIRE_CLASS=<target-class-prefix>   # always
hypr-hands move X Y             # Lua hl.dsp.cursor.move + ±2px verify (exit 4 on mismatch)
hypr-hands click [left|right|middle] [X Y]   # wlrctl; exit 5 = no backend, 3 = locked, 8 = guard
hypr-hands scroll up|down|left|right [steps] # 15 units = 1 wheel notch
hypr-hands drag X1 Y1 X2 Y2 [steps]          # Cua Driver held drag first; JSON says "backend"
HYPR_HANDS_ALLOW_UINPUT=1 hypr-hands drag X1 Y1 X2 Y2   # also allows the ydotool fallback
```
Drag: `hypr-hands check` reports `drag_backend`. `cua-driver-vptr` = Cua Driver desktop-scope drag over the Wayland virtual pointer (one press, held motion, one release); needs the `cua-driver` daemon with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1`. hypr-hands converts logical px to Cua's physical frame, moves to the start, applies the guard and verifies the end (exit 4 mismatch, 11 if Cua fails mid-drag). Auto uses Cua only with one monitor; `HYPR_HANDS_DRAG_BACKEND=cua|ydotool|auto` forces it. Without Cua, ydotool only with `HYPR_HANDS_ALLOW_UINPUT=1`, else exit 5. Modified drags are refused. Duration: `HYPR_HANDS_DRAG_MS` (default 500). A drag takes over the real pointer, so ask first.

Notes: `move` auto-selects Lua `hl.dsp.cursor.move` (Omarchy 4.x) or classic `hyprctl dispatch movecursor X Y` (hyprland.conf setups); classic `dispatch movecursor` fails on Lua-config Hyprland; wlrctl cannot hold a button, so drag uses Cua (or opt-in ydotool). To move windows use `hypr-hands windows`, not drag. Record the cursor first and restore it after.

skills.name: hypr-windows
skills.description: Use to list, focus, move to a workspace, fullscreen, close or wait for windows on the user's Omarchy/Hyprland computer.
skills.content:
---
name: hypr-windows
description: >-
  Use to list, focus, move to a workspace, fullscreen, close or wait for windows
  on the user's Omarchy/Hyprland computer.
---
# Windows (remote)
Run via Shell with the user's Omarchy `machineId`. `ADDR` is optional where shown in brackets (default: the active window).

```bash
hypr-hands windows list                     # JSON: address, class, title, workspace, geometry, floating, fullscreen
hypr-hands windows snapshot [FILE]          # save every window to $XDG_STATE_HOME/hypr-hands/layout-*.json (read-only)
hypr-hands windows restore [FILE]           # put back workspaces, floating, fullscreen, floating pos/size (default: newest snapshot)
hypr-hands windows focus 0xADDR
hypr-hands windows move 0xADDR WS           # to workspace, silently
hypr-hands windows fullscreen [0xADDR]      # toggle; verify .fullscreen 0/2
hypr-hands windows float [0xADDR] [toggle|on|off]
hypr-hands windows resize [0xADDR] W H      # exact px (floating windows)
hypr-hands windows resize [0xADDR] +DX -DY  # relative (tiled windows; any sign makes it relative)
hypr-hands windows moveto [0xADDR] X Y      # exact position, floating windows
hypr-hands windows center [0xADDR]          # floating windows
hypr-hands windows swap [0xADDR] l|r|u|d    # swap with the neighbour
hypr-hands windows movedir [0xADDR] l|r|u|d # move within the layout
hypr-hands windows focusdir l|r|u|d
hypr-hands windows pseudo [0xADDR]          # toggle pseudotile
hypr-hands windows split [0xADDR]           # dwindle togglesplit
hypr-hands windows close 0xADDR             # only windows you opened
hypr-hands wait-window CLASS [timeout]      # after launching an app
```

## Snapshot first, restore offered after
Before any rearranging (float, resize, moveto, center, swap, movedir, move, pseudo, split, fullscreen), run `hypr-hands windows snapshot` and keep the file path it prints. When done, tell the user and offer `hypr-hands windows restore FILE` as an undo. Restore is best effort: tiled windows get their workspace and tiled state back, but exact tiled positions follow the layout; closed windows are listed under `missing`.

## Dispatch forms
Scripts auto-detect the style (`HYPR_HANDS_DISPATCH=lua|classic`; `HYPR_HANDS_DRYRUN=1` prints commands).
- Lua config (Omarchy 4.x): `hyprctl repl "hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.…); return 'ok'"` with `hl.dsp.focus({ window = 'address:0x…' })`, `hl.dsp.focus({ direction = 'l' })`, `hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = 'N', follow = false })`, `hl.dsp.window.float({ action = 'toggle' })`, `hl.dsp.window.resize({ x = W, y = H, relative = false })`, `hl.dsp.window.move({ x = X, y = Y })`, `hl.dsp.window.move({ direction = 'l' })`, `hl.dsp.window.swap({ direction = 'l' })`, `hl.dsp.window.center()`, `hl.dsp.window.pseudo()`, `hl.dsp.layout('togglesplit')`, `hl.dsp.window.fullscreen()`, `hl.dsp.window.close()`.
- Classic `.conf` (Omarchy 3.x): `focuswindow address:0x…`, `movefocus l`, `movetoworkspacesilent N`, `togglefloating`, `resizewindowpixel exact W H,address:0x…`, `movewindowpixel exact X Y,address:0x…`, `movewindow l`, `swapwindow l`, `centerwindow`, `pseudo`, `togglesplit`, `fullscreen 0`, `killactive`.

Launch apps with `setsid uwsm-app -- <app>` (e.g. foot) or `omarchy launch <app>`. Focusing a window on another workspace switches to it. Ask before rearranging the user's windows; afterwards refocus what they had.

skills.name: screen-read
skills.description: Use to read the user's Omarchy/Hyprland screen remotely: screenshots, finding text on screen, clipboard, or a desktop summary.
skills.content:
---
name: screen-read
description: >-
  Use to read the user's Omarchy/Hyprland screen remotely: screenshots, finding
  text on screen, clipboard, or a desktop summary.
---
# Screen read (remote)
Run via Shell with the user's Omarchy `machineId`.

```bash
hypr-hands describe                     # monitors, active window, windows per workspace
hypr-hands shot [full|window|region "X,Y WxH"] [out]   # prints PNG path (physical px)
hypr-hands ocr-find TEXT                # JSON matches with logical centre coords for `click left X Y`
hypr-hands clip get | clip set TEXT
```
To look at a screenshot: Read the printed path with the same `machineId` (or CopyToBox, then Read). Save and restore the user's clipboard if you change it. Screenshots may contain private data; don't upload or share them.

skills.name: omarchy-menus
skills.description: Use to trigger an Omarchy action by name through its keybindings or main menu on the user's Omarchy computer, e.g. 'use the menu to make this window fullscreen'.
skills.content:
---
name: omarchy-menus
description: >-
  Use to trigger an Omarchy action by name through its keybindings or main menu
  on the user's Omarchy computer, e.g. 'use the menu to make this window
  fullscreen'.
---
# Omarchy menus (remote)
Run via Shell with the user's Omarchy `machineId`. Menus are keyboard-filtered lists; no pointer needed.

1. Focus the intended target window first (menu actions apply to it), and set `HYPR_HANDS_REQUIRE_CLASS` to its class.
2. Open: `setsid omarchy-menu-keybindings >/dev/null 2>&1 &` (Super+K) or `omarchy-menu` for the main menu.
3. Confirm the layer is up: `hyprctl layers -j | jq '[.[].levels[][]|.namespace]'` contains `omarchy-menu`. The menu takes keyboard focus while `activewindow` still reports the underlying window.
4. `hypr-hands type 'Full screen'`, check with `hypr-hands shot` / `ocr-find`, then `hypr-hands key Return`.
5. Verify the effect (e.g. `hyprctl clients -j` fullscreen 2 on, 0 off; it's a toggle). Cancel with `hypr-hands key Escape` only while the menu layer is present.
Works the same on Omarchy stable (4.0.0–4.0.5) and edge: `omarchy-menu-keybindings`, `omarchy-menu` and the `omarchy-menu` layer namespace exist in both. Never edit `/usr/share/omarchy`.

skills.name: Cua Driver local computer use
skills.description: Use when driving a real GUI on the user's own computer (especially Omarchy/Hyprland Linux) via the cua-driver CLI over Shell with their machineId, instead of the box desktop.
skills.content:
---
name: Cua Driver local computer use
description: >-
  Use when driving a real GUI on the user's own computer (especially
  Omarchy/Hyprland Linux) via the cua-driver CLI over Shell with their
  machineId, instead of the box desktop.
---
# Cua Driver local computer use

Drive real GUI apps on the **user's registered computer** with the `cua-driver` CLI. Prefer this over the box `computerUse` subagent whenever the task is on their desktop (Omarchy, Hyprland, local apps, signed-in sessions).

Upstream pack (read on demand from the machine being driven): `~/.cua-driver/skills/cua-driver/`: start with `SKILL.md`, then `WORKFLOW.md`, `RUNTIME.md`, and `LINUX.md` on Linux.

Do **not** use for pure filesystem/CLI outcomes doable with Shell/Read. Do not install, upgrade, change permission modes, or reconfigure the daemon unless the user asked.

## Machine and transport
1. Resolve the target with `ListMachines`. Prefer the machine the message came from, or the one the user named.
2. Run every `cua-driver` command with Shell **`machineId` set to that computer**.
3. Ensure `PATH` includes `~/.local/bin`. On Wayland/Hyprland the daemon should run with `CUA_DRIVER_RS_ENABLE_WAYLAND=1` (systemd user unit `cua-driver.service`).
4. Preflight once per session: `cua-driver --version`, `cua-driver status`, `cua-driver doctor`.

If the daemon is down: `systemctl --user start cua-driver.service`. Never `cua-driver stop` a shared service; use `end_session` for your run label. Update: `cua-driver update --apply` then `systemctl --user restart cua-driver.service` (only when the user asks).

Grok Bot does not use stdio MCP for Cua. Use `cua-driver call <tool> '<json>'`.

## Observe → act → verify
Pass the same nonempty session label (not `default`) on every call that accepts `session`.
1. **Find the window**: `list_apps` / `list_windows`; pick by title/app, never blindly the first. `launch_app` only when needed.
2. **Observe**: `get_window_state` with exact `pid` + `window_id`. Prefer `element_token`s from it.
3. **Act once**: `click` / `type_text` / `set_value` with a fresh `element_token` and exact `target: {kind:"window", pid, window_id}`. Default delivery is background. Never invent or reuse stale tokens.
4. **Verify**: fresh `get_window_state` or `verify_state`. A successful exit or `effect:"unverifiable"` is not success.

```bash
cua-driver call list_windows '{}'
cua-driver call get_window_state '{"pid":123,"window_id":456,"session":"run-1"}'
cua-driver call click '{"target":{"kind":"window","pid":123,"window_id":456},"element_token":"…","session":"run-1"}'
cua-driver call end_session '{"session":"run-1"}'
```

## Linux / Hyprland limits
- Background raw input is experimental on Hyprland; prefer AT-SPI tokens. On `background_unavailable`, reobserve and **ask** before foreground or desktop-scope input.
- Desktop-scope drag (`drag` with `"scope":"desktop"`) goes through `zwlr_virtual_pointer_v1`: one press, held motion, one release. Its coordinates are in the **physical** pixel frame of `get_desktop_state`, not Hyprland's logical px (at scale 1.5, logical 200,200 is Cua 300,300). Result is `effect:"unverifiable"`; check it yourself. On Hyprland prefer `hypr-hands drag X1 Y1 X2 Y2` (logical px), which converts, guards and verifies.
- `surface_identity_unproven` on screenshots: don't invent pixels; use tree actions or ask.
- Portal/OS permission dialogs belong to the user.

## Hard rules
1. Exact target every action. 2. Fresh state before and after input. 3. Use returned tokens only. 4. Don't fight the user's focus. 5. Ask before sending, purchases, deletes, permission changes, foreground takeover. 6. Report refusals honestly; no xdotool or fake-click bypasses.

## Pointer/keyboard fallback: hypr-hands
When accessibility can't reach something and the user approved foreground input, use the `hypr-pointer`, `hypr-windows`, `screen-read` skills (`hypr-hands <cmd>`, same machineId) with `HYPR_HANDS_REQUIRE_CLASS` set. `end_session` your cua run first. Drag is Cua desktop drag first, ydotool only as the opt-in fallback.

### Hyprland dispatch: Lua config (Omarchy 4.x) vs classic
Classic `hyprctl dispatch movecursor X Y` fails on Lua-config Hyprland. Use `hyprctl repl`:
```bash
hyprctl repl "hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.cursor.move({ x = 600, y = 400 })); return 'ok'"
hyprctl repl "hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.focus({ window = 'address:0xADDR' })); return 'ok'"
hyprctl repl "hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = '3', follow = false })); return 'ok'"
hyprctl repl "hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.fullscreen()); return 'ok'"
```
Classic equivalents for Hyprland with `hyprland.conf` (Omarchy 3.x, plain Hyprland): `hyprctl dispatch movecursor X Y`, `focuswindow address:0x…`, `movetoworkspacesilent N`, `fullscreen 0`, `killactive`. Omarchy 4.x (stable and edge) uses the Lua form. hypr-hands detects this automatically.

Read-only `hyprctl cursorpos`, `activewindow -j`, `clients -j`, `monitors -j`, `layers -j` work normally. Avoid `hl.dsp.send_shortcut` unless the target is verified focused; it injects real keys.

skills.name: omarchy
skills.description: REQUIRED for end-user customization of Linux desktop, window manager, or system config on Omarchy: ~/.config/hypr/, ~/.config/omarchy/, terminal configs, themes, keybindings, monitors, bar, night light, idle, lock screen, screenshots, reminders. Excludes Omarchy source development.
skills.content:
---
name: omarchy
description: >-
  REQUIRED for end-user customization of Linux desktop, window manager, or
  system config on Omarchy: ~/.config/hypr/, ~/.config/omarchy/, terminal
  configs, themes, keybindings, monitors, bar, night light, idle, lock screen,
  screenshots, reminders. Excludes Omarchy source development.
---
# Omarchy Skill

Manage [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org/) Linux systems - a beautiful, fun, agentic Arch Linux distribution with Hyprland. Adapted from Omarchy's own agent skill (MIT, © David Heinemeier Hansson).

This skill is for end-user customization on installed systems. It is not for contributing to Omarchy source code. Run everything via Shell with the user's Omarchy `machineId`.

## When This Skill MUST Be Used

- Editing ANY file in `~/.config/hypr/` (window rules, animations, keybindings, monitors, etc.)
- Editing `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` (status bar layout, widgets) or anything in `~/.config/omarchy/`
- Editing terminal configs (alacritty, foot, kitty, ghostty)
- Window behavior, animations, opacity, blur, gaps, borders; layer rules, workspaces, monitors
- Themes, backgrounds, fonts, appearance changes
- User-facing `omarchy` commands (`omarchy theme ...`, `omarchy refresh ...`, `omarchy restart ...`)
- Screenshots, screen recording, reminders, night light, idle behavior, lock screen

**Do NOT use this skill for Omarchy development tasks** (editing the Omarchy source tree, creating migrations, or running `omarchy dev ...`).

Omarchy ships deeper topic guides on the machine itself; read them when relevant (e.g. `ls /usr/share/omarchy/` and the packaged agent skill, if present) for Hyprland, shell plugins, theming, hooks and capture.

## Critical Safety Rules

**NEVER modify anything in `/usr/share/omarchy/`** - but READING is safe and encouraged. It is owned by the omarchy package and overwritten on `omarchy update`.

Safe locations: `~/.config/` (user config), `~/.config/omarchy/themes/<custom-name>/` (custom themes), `~/.config/omarchy/hooks/` (automation hooks).

## Privilege Escalation

For an interactive script or command run in a visible terminal, use `sudo`. Use `pkexec` only when the caller cannot interact with a terminal or enter a password there, such as a command launched by an agent. Do not wrap commands that already manage privilege elevation themselves.

## System Architecture

| Component | Purpose | Config Location |
|-----------|---------|-----------------|
| **Arch Linux** | Base OS | `/etc/`, `~/.config/` |
| **Hyprland** | Wayland compositor/WM | `~/.config/hypr/` |
| **Omarchy shell** | Status bar + notifications (Quickshell) | `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` |
| **Launcher/menus** | Quickshell menu | `~/.config/omarchy/extensions/omarchy-menu.jsonc` |
| **Alacritty/Foot/Kitty/Ghostty** | Terminals | `~/.config/<terminal>/` |

## Command Discovery

Omarchy ships a single `omarchy` CLI that dispatches to all `omarchy-*` binaries via `omarchy <group> <action>`. Always prefer this form.

```bash
omarchy commands
omarchy <group> --help
omarchy commands --json
cat $(which omarchy-theme-set)
```

| Group | Purpose | Example |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `omarchy refresh` | Reset config to defaults (backs up first) | `omarchy refresh shell` |
| `omarchy restart` | Restart a service/app | `omarchy restart shell` |
| `omarchy toggle` | Toggle feature on/off | `omarchy toggle nightlight` |
| `omarchy theme` | Theme management | `omarchy theme set <name>` |
| `omarchy bar` | Bar layout and widgets | `omarchy bar move omarchy.clock --section right` |
| `omarchy plugin` | Manage/clone shell plugins | `omarchy plugin clone omarchy.clock` |
| `omarchy hook` | Install automation hooks | `omarchy hook install theme-set <script>` |
| `omarchy install` | Install optional software | `omarchy install docker dbs` |
| `omarchy launch` | Launch apps | `omarchy launch browser` |
| `omarchy capture` | Screenshots and recordings | `omarchy capture screenshot` |
| `omarchy reminder` | Desktop notification reminders | `omarchy reminder 15 "Stretch"` |
| `omarchy pkg` | Package management | `omarchy pkg add <pkg>` |
| `omarchy setup` | Interactive setup wizards | `omarchy setup security fingerprint` |
| `omarchy update` | System updates | `omarchy update` |

## Configuration Locations

Hyprland: `~/.config/hypr/` (Omarchy 4.x uses Lua files such as `bindings.lua`, `monitors.lua`, `looknfeel.lua`). Shell: `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json`. Terminals: `~/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml`, `~/.config/foot/foot.ini`, `~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf`, `~/.config/ghostty/config` (apply with `omarchy restart terminal`). Others: btop `~/.config/btop/btop.conf`, fastfetch `~/.config/fastfetch/config.jsonc`, lazygit `~/.config/lazygit/config.yml`, starship `~/.config/starship.toml`, git `~/.config/git/config`.

## Safe Customization Pattern

```bash
cat ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua
cp ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua.bak.$(date +%s)
# make changes, then:
hyprctl reload && hyprctl configerrors
```
Shell config and `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/` hot-reload on save.

**Reset to defaults (`omarchy refresh shell`, `omarchy refresh hyprland`) - ALWAYS get user confirmation first.**

## System Commands

```bash
omarchy update
omarchy version
omarchy debug --no-sudo --print   # ALWAYS use these flags
omarchy system lock | shutdown | reboot
omarchy refresh config <config-file>   # path relative to ~/.config/
omarchy reinstall   # nuclear option, confirm first
```

## Decision Framework

1. Stock omarchy command? Use it directly.
2. Config edit? Edit in `~/.config/`, never `/usr/share/omarchy/`.
3. Package install? `omarchy pkg add <pkgs...>` (or `omarchy pkg aur add`), in a terminal the user can type their password into.
4. Unsure? Run `omarchy commands` or `omarchy <group> --help`.

## Example Requests

- "Change my theme to catppuccin" -> `omarchy theme set catppuccin`
- "Add a keybinding for Super+E to open the file manager" -> check bindings, then `o.rebind` or `o.bind` in `~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua`
- "Configure my external monitor" -> edit `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua`
- "Make the window gaps smaller" -> edit `~/.config/hypr/looknfeel.lua`
- "Turn on night light" -> `omarchy toggle nightlight`
- "Lock after ten minutes" -> set `idle.lock` to `600` in `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json`
- "Reset shell/bar to defaults" -> `omarchy refresh shell` (confirm first)

## Out of Scope

Editing files in `/usr/share/omarchy/`, creating or editing migrations, running `omarchy dev ...`.
